completed_items: Added a fail-closed HTTPS WSGI API with short-lived issuer/audience-bound HS256 bearer verification, rotated key ids, expiry and session revocation checks
Added authenticated per-account workout history and progress summary contracts
Added stable client record versioning, idempotency conflict detection, provenance validation and server-side deduplication
Added sets, reps, load, rest, RPE, RIR, personal-record and volume persistence
Added server-authoritative competition claim comparison against stored workout facts
Rejected client-supplied account identity and rejected unknown workout fields
Documented the production runtime variables with no development key or insecure endpoint fallback
blockers: The V2 API source is tested but is not deployed to a persistent HTTPS runtime, so no authenticated production sync claim is made.
The existing AppDeploy origin returns the SPA HTML for /v2/workouts:sync and cannot be bound as the V2 API endpoint.
AppDeploy paused new deployments because fewer than 14 free daily credits remained; its reported reset is 2026-10-03T00:00:00Z.
Production auth issuer, audience, key ring and durable database configuration have not been provisioned to a V2 runtime.

The packaged V2 offline client does not yet acquire a production account access token; it exposes a non-persistent native token handoff boundary, but the current Product JavaScript does not invoke it.
next_action: After the free deployment quota resets, deploy a backend-only V2 route on the existing authorized persistent runtime (or another authorized persistent HTTPS host), configure its production auth and durable store, implement and test a secure account-token handoff into the Android bridge, run authenticated sync/history/progress/competition probes, then set THF_FITNESS_V2_BASE_URL and rebuild the exact Android candidate.
